Hi Olivia / Jake —

Great to meet you yesterday. Per our conversation, I wanted to put an early outline on paper for a dedicated retainer (reserved capacity) engagement. High-level ask from your side: support sustained production LLM inference for conversational and retrieval-augmented workflows, with long-context sessions (8k–12k tokens typical) and a small number of high-concurrency agents during peak windows.

Can you confirm the following so we can build an accurate capacity plan?
- Target peak QPS / concurrent sessions you expect (p95 and expected average)
- Primary model(s) you plan to serve (open model name or custom fine-tune) and desired context length per session
- Any hard latency SLOs (e.g., token/response latency targets) or mandatory quantization constraints for model fidelity
- Procurement timeline and any gating (PO, SOC 2 evidence, contract language)

We can provide two parallel sizing options: a conservative (no quantization) footprint and an optimized (int8/int4 + KV offload) footprint — both with recommended GPU types and a canary plan. Attaching a short retainer outline for scope & pricing bands.

Attachments: retainer-outline.pdf (scope & sample pricing bands)

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if helpful.

Thanks Sean — quick answers below and attaching a consolidated requirements sheet.

- Peak: ~60 requests/sec sustained for a 2-hour daily window (business hours), with spikes to 120 req/s for short bursts (10–15 minutes). Average during other hours ~12 req/s.
- Concurrent active sessions: ~220 active conversations during peak, dropping to ~40 off-peak.
- Model(s): evaluating two variants — a 34B encoder-decoder we trained in FP16 (we call it BCL-34B) and a distilled 8B variant for cost-sensitive fallbacks. We expect to route <30% traffic to 34B initially and scale as we validate quality.
- Context: canonical sessions average 8k tokens; 95th ~12k including retrieval context.
- Latency SLO: interactive responses preferred under 800ms for full-turn (end-to-end). Token-level latency target is lower but we care most about turn latency.
- Quantization: we'd like to know what we can safely do without regressing quality — if int8/int4 reduces GPU count meaningfully, that helps the commercial case.
- Procurement: target signature by end of September; procurement wants an estimated monthly committed spend for budgeting.

Attachments: BC_requirements.xlsx

Appreciate the two-scenario approach — can you include KV cache sizing guidance? We're worried long contexts will blow up GPU memory even with quantization.

—Olivia

Hi Olivia — pulled together two capacity scenarios and a short explainer on KV cache sizing. High-level assumptions (please confirm or correct):
- Primary traffic mix: 30% 34B (FP16), 70% 8B fallback (FP16).
- Peak r/s: 120 req/s burst, 60 sustained (as noted).
- Average turn = 400 tokens generated per request; we assume ~500k generated tokens/day for planning.

Scenario A — Conservative (no quantization, FP16 runtime):
- Model memory (approx): BCL-34B FP16 weights ~68GB resident (including optimizer-free format & reserve for kernel memory).
- KV cache: For 12k context, KV cache delta ~ 24 bytes per token for a 34B model compressed format (router + keys/values) => ~288KB per 12k-token session. For 220 concurrent sessions at peak that is ~63GB of KV memory if kept entirely in GPU DRAM.
- Effective per-GPU concurrency (H100 80GB): ~6–8 concurrent 34B sessions with amortized prompt cache and batching tuned for interactive latency. To serve 220 concurrent sessions (30% to 34B => ~66 sessions), we'd need ~9–11 H100 GPUs dedicated to 34B (plus extra for headroom/autoscale), and separate smaller nodes for 8B traffic.

Scenario B — Optimized (int8 inference + KV offload to managed cache + prefix caching):
- Model weights quantized (int8 dynamic) reduce model resident to ~26–32GB on GPU for the 34B variant (depends on quant recipe).
- KV offload: store cold KV shards in a fast host-local or NVMe-backed cache and keep only working sets in GPU DRAM; aggressive prefix caching keeps the top 2–3k tokens per active session in GPU, rest paged to NVMe. For a 12k context worst-case this reduces GPU KV footprint to ~12–15GB total for the 66 34B sessions.
- With int8 + KV offload, per-GPU concurrency on H100 (or A100x80) can increase to ~12–16 34B sessions; that implies we can provision ~4–6 GPUs for the 34B portion instead of 9–11 in Scenario A.

Tradeoffs & recommendations:
- Quality: int8 can be safe for many workloads but expect a small (low single-digit %) delta vs FP16 on some instruction-heavy prompts. We recommend a short eval suite (10–20 representative prompts) against both configs to quantify regression before committing.
- Latency: KV offload adds tail latency risk on cache misses; mitigate with warmed-on-write prefetch and hybrid NVMe->DRAM staging. For your 800ms turn SLO we recommend conservative warming for the first 48–72 hours post-deploy and a canary with synthetic traffic.
- Pricing: I attached cost-scenarios.pdf with committed-monthly bands and an example structure: 4–6 GPUs reserved for 34B in optimized mode vs 10–12 in conservative. We will draft exact monthly commitment ranges once Marcus inputs commercial uplift.

Attachments referenced: kvcache_sizing_v1.xlsx (per-token math & concurrency model), cost-scenarios.pdf

Next steps: if these assumptions match, I'll model an exact GPU-count + commit band and produce a sample SOW. Marcus — can you add committed pricing bands and any discount tiers we should consider for a 12-month retainer?

Best,
